title: The Debt of Vienna
premise: Jonah Thackeray, a crash investigator haunted by the unexplained death of his family in row twelve, is pulled into a case that officially never happened: a passenger flight whose records vanish mid-flight over Central Europe. The trail leads to Lena Vogel, a defector carrying proof that a powerful Vienna-based consortium engineered the disappearance to bury its crimes—and that Jonah's family was an earlier casualty of the same machine. As dawn approaches, Jonah must extract Lena from Vienna before her flight leaves, knowing she may be bait designed to draw out anyone who remembers row twelve. In the end, Jonah chooses love and truth over duty, exposing the consortium at the cost of his anonymity, and finally learns what really happened to his family.
about_author: E. M. Pemberton is the pen name of a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade reviewing accident reports across Europe before turning to fiction. They write from a farmhouse in the Carpathian foothills, where the night sky still fills with flight paths.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Opening on the anniversary of his family's deaths, Jonah works a routine crash file he can't close, haunted by inconsistencies in row twelve. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into obsession; establishes his compulsion to find causes no one wants named.

chapters.title: The Case That Isn't
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A colleague slips him a fragment: flight OS-114 logged a distress call, then every record evaporated while the plane was airborne. His supervisor orders him to drop it. Beat: unease curdling into defiance as Jonah realizes the erasure was deliberate.

chapters.title: Ghost Manifest
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Reconstructing the manifest from boarding scans, Jonah finds one name flagged and scrubbed: Lena Vogel. A watcher follows him home. Beat: paranoia arrives; the invisible man discovers invisibility is a service others provide—for a price.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Archive
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Hiding in Vienna under borrowed papers, Lena reveals she copied consortium files proving OS-114 was downed to destroy evidence against them. She knows someone will come for her—she only hopes it's not them. Beat: fear braided with resolve.

chapters.title: Vienna After Midnight
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Following the manifest thread to Vienna, Jonah makes contact through a disgraced archivist, Marta. First glimpse of Lena at a distance. Beat: cautious alliance; two people who trust nothing recognize the same wound in each other.

chapters.title: What the Consortium Buys
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marta explains the network: officials, insurers, a private intelligence arm called Meridian that makes disasters 'unattributable.' Jonah realizes row twelve fits their pattern. Beat: horror of scale; personal grief reframed as systemic crime.

chapters.title: Safehouse, Unsafe Hours
chapters.summary: Lena and Jonah's shared POV. Holed up together, they trade stories—her brother disappeared by Meridian, his family in row twelve. Tenderness sparks between duty-bound strangers. Beat: intimacy against instinct; love beginning where vigilance should be.

chapters.title: The Tail
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A Meridian operative, Kessler, corners Jonah with an offer: walk away, keep his pension, forget. Jonah refuses and barely escapes. Beat: the point of no return; his old life formally ends in a rain-slick alley.

chapters.title: Files That Breathe
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Decoding her copies, Lena finds a second list: future flights marked for 'attribution management,' including one departing Vienna at dawn—with her name on the manifest. Beat: dread; the escape route is the trap.

chapters.title: Bait Confirmed
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Cross-checking, Jonah confirms the dawn flight is staged: Meridian wants Lena extracted publicly so her death can be blamed on foreign agents—and anyone helping her dies with her. Beat: cold clarity; he tells her anyway, and she chooses to fly regardless.

chapters.title: Marta's Price
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta agrees to forge credentials but demands the full archive go public, whatever it costs. Old loyalties surface—she once worked for Meridian. Beat: guilt and redemption; the cost of belonging to something corrupt.

chapters.title: Kessler's Ledger
chapters.summary: Kessler's POV. Inside Meridian, Kessler begins doubting the operation when ordered to ensure civilian casualties. Flashbacks to disasters he made unattributable. Beat: corruption examined from within; a man realizing power has spent him like currency.

chapters.title: The Ringstrasse Run
chapters.summary: Jonah and Lena's POV. Moving safehouses through Vienna, they're ambushed; Marta is wounded covering their escape. Beat: action and loss; the plan's first blood, and Jonah's terror of losing someone again.

chapters.title: Confessions at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Lena and Jonah's POV. Waiting out a lockdown, they confess everything—Lena's survivor guilt, Jonah's fantasy that finding the cause could bring his family back. Beat: emotional climax of the relationship; love stated plainly, without promise of tomorrow.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Offer
chapters.summary: Kessler's POV. Kessler secretly contacts Jonah with a partial ledger, offering defection of his own—but the meeting is a test Jonah must pass without knowing it. Beat: shifting alliances; trust as a weapon aimed at both sides.

chapters.title: Airport of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Recon of Schwechat airport reveals Meridian's kill team embedded among ground crew. Jonah maps a route through cargo tunnels. Beat: tactical tension; the clock becomes the antagonist as dawn nears.

chapters.title: Everything Burns Brightest Before
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena insists on triggering the archive release mid-extraction so her death can't erase the truth. She and Jonah agree: if separated, no one waits. Beat: sacrifice embraced; duty and love briefly pointing the same direction.

chapters.title: Dawn Extraction
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The extraction erupts—cargo tunnels, gunfire, Kessler turning his weapon on Meridian at the decisive moment. Jonah reaches the gate as the plane doors close. Beat: climax; chaos, betrayal reversed, and a choice made in seconds.

chapters.title: Row Twelve, Answered
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Aboard, Lena shows him the decoded file: row twelve was Meridian's first test of unattributable downing. Grief and vindication collide. Beat: catharsis; the question that defined him finally answered, and it doesn't heal—it clarifies.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The archive goes public; governments move, Meridian fractures, Kessler surrenders his ledger. Some names are protected, some fall. Beat: consequence; power exposed but not fully destroyed—the corruption retreats rather than dies.

chapters.title: The Debt of Vienna
chapters.summary: Jonah and Lena's POV. Weeks later, in a safe house outside Prague, they settle what they owe each other and the dead: testimony, memory, a life continued together. Beat: quiet resolution; belonging chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Flight Paths
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, epilogue. Jonah testifies before a tribunal, then watches evening traffic trace luminous lines over the city—no longer hunting causes, but guarding truths. Final line echoes row twelve. Beat: peace earned, vigilance kept; love as the duty he chose.
